vsm1.4:180.1:
Once this has been obtained in this way, and once he has mastery in the five ways already
described, then on emerging from the now familiar third jhāna,
vsm1.4:180.2:
he can regard the flaws in it thus: “This attainment is threatened by the nearness of happiness;
‘Whatever there is in it of mental concern about bliss proclaims its grossness’ (D I 37; see Ch. IX, n. 20),
vsm1.4:180.3: and its factors are weakened by the grossness of the bliss so expressed.”
vsm1.4:180.4: He can bring the fourth jhāna to mind as quieter
vsm1.4:180.5: and so end his attachment to the third jhāna and set about doing what is needed for attaining the fourth.
vsm1.4:181.1:
When he has emerged from the third jhāna, the bliss, in other words, the mental joy, appears
gross to him as he reviews the jhāna factors with mindfulness and full awareness,
vsm1.4:181.2:
while the equanimity as feeling and the unification of mind appear peaceful. Then, as he brings that same sign to mind as “earth,
earth” again and again with the purpose of abandoning the gross factor and obtaining the peaceful factors,
vsm1.4:181.3: knowing “now the fourth jhāna will arise,”
vsm1.4:181.4: there arises in him mind-door adverting with that same earth kasiṇa as its object, interrupting the life-continuum.
vsm1.4:181.5: After that either four or five impulsions impel on that same object,
vsm1.4:181.6: the last one of which is an impulsion of the fine-material sphere belonging to the fourth jhāna.
vsm1.4:181.7: The rest are of the kinds already stated (§74).
vsm1.4:182.1:
But there is this difference: blissful (pleasant) feeling is not a condition,
as repetition condition, for neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling,
vsm1.4:182.2: and the preliminary work must be aroused in the case of the fourth jhāna with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling;
vsm1.4:182.3: consequently these consciousnesses of the preliminary work are associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling,
vsm1.4:182.4: and here happiness vanishes simply owing to their association with equanimity.
vsm1.4:183.1: And at this point, “With the abandoning of pleasure and pain
vsm1.4:183.2: and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief
vsm1.4:183.3:
he enters upon and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure
and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity” (Vibh 245),
vsm1.4:183.4: and so he has attained the fourth jhāna, which abandons one factor, possesses two factors,
vsm1.4:183.5: is good in three ways, possesses ten characteristics, and is of the earth kasiṇa.
vsm1.4:184.1: Herein, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain: with the abandoning of bodily pleasure and bodily pain.
vsm1.4:184.2: With the previous: which took place before, not in the moment of the fourth jhāna.
vsm1.4:184.3: Disappearance of joy and grief: with the previous disappearance of the two, that is, mental bliss (pleasure) and mental pain;
vsm1.4:184.4: with the abandoning, is what is meant.
vsm1.4:185.1: But when does the abandoning of these take place?
vsm1.4:185.2: At the moment of access of the four jhānas.
vsm1.4:185.3: For mental joy is only abandoned at the moment of the fourth-jhāna access,
vsm1.4:185.4:
while bodily pain, mental grief, and bodily bliss (pleasure) are abandoned
respectively at the moments of access of the first, second, and third jhānas.
vsm1.4:185.5: So although the order in which they are abandoned is not actually mentioned,
vsm1.4:185.6:
nevertheless the abandoning of the pleasure, pain, joy, and grief, is stated here
according to the order in which the faculties are summarized in the Indriya Vibhaṅga (Vibh 122).
vsm1.4:186.1: But if these are only abandoned at the moments of access of the several jhānas,
vsm1.4:186.2:
why is their cessation said to. take place in the jhāna itself in the following
passage: “And where does the arisen pain faculty cease without remainder?
vsm1.4:186.3:
Here, bhikkhus, quite secluded from sense desires, secluded from unprofitable things,
a bhikkhu enters upon and dwells in the first jhāna, which is … born of seclusion.
vsm1.4:186.4: It is here that the arisen pain faculty ceases without remainder …
vsm1.4:186.5:
Where does the arisen grief faculty cease without remainder? … in the second jhāna … Where does the arisen pleasure
faculty cease without remainder? … in the third jhāna … Where does the arisen joy faculty cease without remainder?
vsm1.4:186.6:
Here, bhikkhus, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief
a bhikkhu enters upon and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which … has mindfulness purified by equanimity.
vsm1.4:186.7: It is here that the arisen joy faculty ceases without remainder” (S V 213–15) evaṃ jhānesveva nirodho vutto?
vsm1.4:186.8: It is said in that way there referring to reinforced cessation.
vsm1.4:186.9: For in the first jhāna, etc., it is their reinforced cessation, not just their cessation, that takes place.
vsm1.4:186.10: At the moment of access it is just their cessation, not their reinforced cessation, that takes place.
vsm1.4:187.1: For accordingly, during the first jhāna access, which has multiple adverting,
vsm1.4:187.2: there could be rearising of the bodily pain faculty due to contact with gadflies, flies, etc.
vsm1.4:187.3: or the discomfort of an uneven seat, though that pain faculty had already ceased, but not so during absorption.
vsm1.4:187.4: Or else, though it has ceased during access, it has not absolutely ceased there since it is not quite beaten out by opposition.
vsm1.4:187.5: But during absorption the whole body is showered with bliss owing to pervasion by happiness.
vsm1.4:187.6: And the pain faculty has absolutely ceased in one whose body is showered with bliss, since it is beaten out then by opposition.
vsm1.4:188.1:
And during the second-jhāna access too, which has multiple advertings, there could
be rearising of the mental grief faculty, although it had already ceased there,
vsm1.4:188.2:
because it arises when there is bodily weariness and mental vexation, which have applied
thought and sustained thought as their condition,
vsm1.4:188.3: but it does not arise when applied and sustained thought are absent.
vsm1.4:188.4: When it arises, it does so in the presence of applied and sustained thought, and they are not abandoned in the second-jhāna access;
vsm1.4:188.5: but this is not so in the second jhāna itself because its conditions are abandoned there.
vsm1.4:189.1: Likewise in the third-jhāna access there could be rearising of the abandoned bodily pleasure faculty
vsm1.4:189.2: in one whose body was pervaded by the superior materiality originated by the consciousness associated with the happiness.
vsm1.4:189.3: But not so in the third jhāna itself.
vsm1.4:189.4: For in the third jhāna the happiness that is a condition for the bodily bliss (pleasure) has ceased entirely.
vsm1.4:189.5: Likewise in the fourth-jhāna access there could be re-arising of the abandoned mental joy faculty
vsm1.4:189.6:
because of its nearness and because it has not been properly surmounted
owing to the absence of equanimity brought to absorption strength.
vsm1.4:189.7: But not so in the fourth jhāna itself.
vsm1.4:189.8: And that is why in each case (§186) the words “without remainder” are included thus:
vsm1.4:189.9: “It is here that the arisen pain faculty ceases without remainder.”
vsm1.4:190.1: Here it may be asked: Then if these kinds of feeling are abandoned in the access in this way, why are they brought in here?
vsm1.4:190.2: It is done so that they can be readily grasped.
vsm1.4:190.3: For the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling described here by the words “which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure” is subtle,
vsm1.4:190.4: hard to recognize and not readily grasped.
vsm1.4:190.5: So just as, when a cattle-herd wants to catch a refractory ox that cannot be caught at all by approaching it,
vsm1.4:190.6: he collects all the cattle into one pen
vsm1.4:190.7: and lets them out one by one,
vsm1.4:190.8:
and then he says “That is it; catch it,” and so it gets caught as well, so too the Blessed One has collected
all these five kinds of feeling together so that they can be grasped readily;
vsm1.4:190.9:
for when they are shown collected together in this way, then what is not bodily
pleasure (bliss) or bodily pain or mental joy or mental grief
vsm1.4:190.10: can still be grasped in this way: “This is neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.”
vsm1.4:191.1: Besides, this may be understood as said in order to show the condition for the neither-painful-nor-pleasant mind-deliverance.
vsm1.4:191.2: For the abandoning of bodily pain, etc., are conditions for that,
vsm1.4:191.3:
according as it is said: “There are four conditions, friend, for the attainment
of the neither-painful-nor-pleasant mind-deliverance.
vsm1.4:191.4:
Here, friend, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief
a bhikkhu enters upon and dwells in the fourth jhāna … equanimity.
vsm1.4:191.5: These are the four conditions for the attainment of the neither-painful-nor-pleasant mind-deliverance” (M I 296).
vsm1.4:192.1:
Or alternatively, just as, although mistaken view of individuality, etc., have already been abandoned in the earlier paths,
they are nevertheless mentioned as abandoned in the description of the third path for the purpose of recommending it (cf. §155),
vsm1.4:192.2: so too these kinds of feeling can be understood as mentioned here for the purpose of recommending this jhāna.
vsm1.4:192.3: Or alternatively, they can be understood as mentioned for the purpose of showing that greed and hate are very far away
vsm1.4:192.4: owing to the removal of their conditions;
vsm1.4:192.5: for of these, pleasure (bliss) is a condition for joy, and joy for greed;
vsm1.4:192.6: pain is a condition for grief and grief for hate.
vsm1.4:192.7: So with the removal of pleasure (bliss), etc., greed and hate are very far away since they are removed along with their conditions.
vsm1.4:193.1: Which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure: no pain owing to absence of pain; no pleasure owing to absence of pleasure (bliss).
vsm1.4:193.2: By this he indicates the third kind of feeling
vsm1.4:193.3: that is in opposition both to pain and to pleasure, not the mere absence of pain and pleasure.
vsm1.4:193.4: This third kind of feeling named neither-pain-nor-pleasure is also called “equanimity.”
vsm1.4:193.5: It has the characteristic of experiencing what is contrary to both the desirable and the undesirable.
vsm1.4:193.8: Its proximate cause should be understood as the cessation of pleasure (bliss).
vsm1.4:194.1: And has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity: has purity of mindfulness brought about by equanimity.
vsm1.4:194.2: For the mindfulness in this jhāna is quite purified, and its purification is effected by equanimity, not by anything else.
vsm1.4:194.3: That is why it is said to have purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.
vsm1.4:194.4: Also it is said in the Vibhaṅga: “This mindfulness is cleared, purified, clarified, by equanimity;
vsm1.4:194.5: hence it is said to have purity of mindfulness due to equanimity” (Vibh 261).
vsm1.4:194.6: And the equanimity due to which there comes to be this purity of mindfulness should be understood as specific neutrality in meaning.
vsm1.4:194.7: And not only mindfulness is purified by it here, but also all associated states.
vsm1.4:194.8: However, the teaching is given under the heading of mindfulness.
vsm1.4:195.1: Herein, this equanimity exists in the three lower jhānas too;
vsm1.4:195.2:
but just as, although a crescent moon exists by day but is not purified or clear since it is outshone by the sun’s
radiance in the daytime or since it is deprived of the night, which is its ally owing to gentleness and owing to helpfulness to it,
vsm1.4:195.3:
so too, this crescent moon of equanimity consisting in specific neutrality exists in the first jhāna,
etc., but it is not purified since it is outshone by the glare of the opposing states consisting in applied thought,
etc., and since it is deprived of the night of equanimity-as-feeling for its ally.
vsm1.4:195.4: And because it is not purified,
vsm1.4:195.5: the conascent mindfulness and other states are not purified either, like the unpurified crescent moon’s radiance by day.
vsm1.4:195.6: That is why no one among these first three jhānas is said to have purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.
vsm1.4:195.7:
But here this crescent moon consisting in specific neutrality is utterly pure because it is not outshone by the glare
of the opposing states consisting in applied thought, etc., and because it has the night of equanimity-as-feeling for its ally.
vsm1.4:195.9: the conascent mindfulness and other states are purified and clear also, like the purified crescent moon’s radiance.
vsm1.4:195.10: That, it should be understood, is why only this jhāna is said to have purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.
vsm1.4:196.1: Fourth: it is fourth in numerical series;
vsm1.4:196.2: and it is fourth because it is entered upon fourth.
vsm1.4:197.1: Then it was said, which abandons one factor, possesses two factors (§183);
vsm1.4:197.2: here the abandoning of the one factor should be understood as the abandoning of joy.
vsm1.4:197.3: But that joy is actually abandoned in the first impulsions of the same cognitive series (cf. §185).
vsm1.4:197.4: Hence it is called its factor of abandoning.
vsm1.4:197.5:
The possession of the two factors should be understood as the arising of the two,
namely, equanimity as feeling and unification of mind.
vsm1.4:197.6: The rest is as stated in the case of the first jhāna.
vsm1.4:197.7: This, in the first place, is according to the fourfold reckoning of jhāna.
vsm1.4:198.1: When, however, he is developing fivefold jhāna, then, on emerging from the now familiar first jhāna,
vsm1.4:198.2:
he can regard the flaws in it in this way: “This attainment is threatened by the nearness of the hindrances,
and its factors are weakened by the grossness of applied thought.”
vsm1.4:198.3: He can bring the second jhāna to mind as quieter
vsm1.4:198.4: and so end his attachment to the first jhāna and set about doing what is needed for attaining the second.
vsm1.4:199.1: Now, he emerges from the first jhāna mindfully and fully aware;
vsm1.4:199.2: and only applied thought appears gross to him as he reviews the jhāna factors, while the sustained thought, etc., appear peaceful.
vsm1.4:199.3:
Then, as he brings that same sign to mind as “earth, earth” again and again with the purpose of abandoning
the gross factor and obtaining the peaceful factors,
vsm1.4:199.4: the second jhāna arises in him in the way already described.
vsm1.4:199.5: Its factor of abandoning is applied thought only.
vsm1.4:199.6: The four beginning with sustained thought are the factors that it possesses.
vsm1.4:199.7: The rest is as already stated.
vsm1.4:200.1:
When this has been obtained in this way, and once he has mastery in the five ways already
described, then on emerging from the now familiar second jhāna
vsm1.4:200.2:
he can regard the flaws in it in this way: “This attainment is threatened by the nearness of applied
thought, and its factors are weakened by the grossness of sustained thought.”
vsm1.4:200.3: He can bring the third jhāna to mind as quieter
vsm1.4:200.4: and so end his attachment to the second jhāna and set about doing what is needed for attaining the third.
vsm1.4:201.1: Now, he emerges from the second jhāna mindfully and fully aware;
vsm1.4:201.2: only sustained thought appears gross to him as he reviews the jhāna factors, while happiness, etc., appear peaceful.
vsm1.4:201.3:
Then, as he brings that same sign to mind as “earth, earth” again and again with the purpose of abandoning
the gross factor and obtaining the peaceful factors,
vsm1.4:201.4: the third jhāna arises in him in the way already described.
vsm1.4:201.5: Its factor of abandoning is sustained thought only.
vsm1.4:201.6: The three beginning with happiness, as in the second jhāna in the fourfold reckoning, are the factors that it possesses.
vsm1.4:201.7: The rest is as already stated.
vsm1.4:202.1: So that which is the second in the fourfold reckoning
vsm1.4:202.2: becomes the second and third in the fivefold reckoning by being divided into two.
vsm1.4:202.3: And those which are the third and fourth in the former reckoning become the fourth and fifth in this reckoning.
vsm1.4:202.4: The first remains the first in each case.
vsm1.4:202.5:
The fourth chapter called “The Description of the Earth Kasiṇa” in the Treatise on the Development
of Concentration in the Path of Purification composed for the purpose of gladdening good people.
